title: Tree-unrolling preserves evaluation
statement: Let $F$ be a layered Boolean circuit with input nodes indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and output type $\mathrm{out}$. Suppose each non-input node is designated AND or OR, every gate has finite arity, and each gate computes the conjunction of its input values when designated AND and their disjunction when designated OR. Then for every output node $o$ and every Boolean input assignment $x$, the tree circuit obtained by unrolling $o$ evaluates to the same value as $F$ at $o$ under $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a layered Boolean circuit from $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ to $\mathrm{out}$
Each non-input node has an AND-or-OR designation
Each gate computes the designated conjunction or disjunction of its inputs
$x$ is a Boolean assignment to the $n$ inputs
replaced:
Let $F$ be a Boolean feedforward circuit with input variables indexed by
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and output nodes of type $\mathrm{out}$, equipped with a flag
assigning to each non-input node the label AND or OR and a witness that each gate has
finite arity. Suppose $F$ is an AND/OR circuit: every gate computes the conjunction of
the values on its input wires when its node is labelled AND, and their disjunction when
it is labelled OR. Then for every output node $o$ and every assignment $x :
\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, the tree-shaped Boolean circuit obtained by unrolling $o$
from the last layer down to the inputs, evaluated at $x$, agrees with the value that $F$
itself assigns to $o$ under the input assignment $x$.
